blocks.heading: What this section covers
blocks.text: Define market failure, and settle the key terms around it: public good, merit good, demerit good, private, external and social costs, and private, external and social benefits.

blocks.heading: Market failure, defined
blocks.text: Market failure is the failure of the price mechanism, left to itself, to allocate resources in the way that best serves society: some goods are produced at levels above what their full effects on others justify, and others at levels below what those effects warrant. A lighthouse on the coast of Portugal shows the idea: ships within sight of the beam use it whatever they paid, so the light's benefits never reach the price, and private builders tend to put up too few.

blocks.heading: Private, external and social costs
blocks.text: A private cost is a cost the decision-maker pays directly: the diesel a Windhoek bus operator burns is a private cost. An external cost is imposed on people outside the transaction and goes unpaid by them: the exhaust pedestrians breathe is a cost the operator never settles. A social cost is the two together, the full cost of the activity to society. The benefits mirror this: a private benefit lands on the buyer, an external benefit on people outside the transaction, and a social benefit on both combined.

blocks.heading: Public goods, merit goods, demerit goods
blocks.text: A public good has two features. Its benefits cannot be confined to those who pay - street lighting over Katutura's taxi ranks lights the non-payer as surely as the payer - and one person's use of it leaves as much for the next. A merit good, such as schooling or vaccination, is one whose benefits consumers tend to undervalue, so too little is bought. A demerit good, such as tobacco or strong drink, is one whose harm consumers tend to undercount, so too much is bought.

blocks.heading: Market failure is not business failure
blocks.text: The confusion learners make: market failure sounds like a firm going under. The boundary: business failure is one firm closing because it cannot cover its costs; market failure is a whole market settling at the wrong level of output, even while its firms trade on. The test: ask whether the statement is about a single firm's survival or a whole market's level of output. When Etosha Gate Lodge shuts its gates after two quiet seasons, that is business failure; when too little is spent on Walvis Bay's flood defences, that is market failure.

blocks.heading: Connections
blocks.text: The price mechanism this topic questions was built in topics 2.3 (demand) and 2.4 (supply), whose meeting sets the market price and the level of output this topic examines.
